title: Nehemiah 11: Repopulating the Holy City
body:
Read the chapter → [Nehemiah 11](/bible/nehemiah/11)

## Introduction

This session covers the last three chapters of Nehemiah and then opens the book of Esther. [Nehemiah 11](/bible/nehemiah/11) and 12 are largely registers of names, the record of who came back and settled Jerusalem, who served as priests and Levites, and how they dedicated the wall with thanksgiving and singing. These are our ancestors, and this is the book of records; a man's name has to be found written in the book to have a part in the inheritance. [Nehemiah 13](/bible/nehemiah/13) turns to reform, cutting off the mixed multitude, guarding the Sabbath from buying and selling, and putting away strange wives that had turned the people's hearts and their children's speech away from the law. The thread through it all is order restored according to the covenant given by Moses. Read these chapters as the record of a people applying their laws again once they came back into their land.

**[Nehemiah 11:1-2](/bible/nehemiah/11#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/nehemiah/11#v1)</sup> And the rulers of the people dwelt at Jerusalem: the rest of the people also cast lots, to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem the holy city, and nine parts to dwell in other cities.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/nehemiah/11#v2)</sup> And the people blessed all the men, that willingly offered themselves to dwell at Jerusalem.

- The rulers of the people dwelt at Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one of ten to dwell in the holy city, while nine parts remained in the other cities.
- This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10, where the people entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of Moses, keep the Sabbath, and not marry the people of the land. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done.

  - **[Nehemiah 10:29](/bible/nehemiah/10#v29)**
    > <sup>[29](/bible/nehemiah/10#v29)</sup> They clave to their brethren, their nobles, and entered into a curse, and into an oath, to walk in God’s law, which was given by Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the Lord our Lord, and his judgments and his statutes;

    The people clave to their nobles and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in God's law given by Moses and to do all his commandments.
  - **[Nehemiah 10:30](/bible/nehemiah/10#v30)**
    > <sup>[30](/bible/nehemiah/10#v30)</sup> And that we would not give our daughters unto the people of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons:

    Part of that oath was that they would not give their daughters to the people of the land nor take their daughters for their sons.
  - **[Nehemiah 10:31](/bible/nehemiah/10#v31)**
    > <sup>[31](/bible/nehemiah/10#v31)</sup> And if the people of the land bring ware or any victuals on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day: and that we would leave the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt.

    They also swore not to buy victuals from the people of the land on the Sabbath day, the same Sabbath commerce Nehemiah later has to enforce in chapter 13.
  - **[Isaiah 3:16-17](/bible/isaiah/3#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/isaiah/3#v16)</sup> Moreover the Lord saith, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet:
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/isaiah/3#v17)</sup> Therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will discover their secret parts.

    As the holy city is filled again, the haughtiness of the daughters of Zion is a warning against pride and outward vanity in the restored people.

**[Nehemiah 11:3-9](/bible/nehemiah/11#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/nehemiah/11#v3)</sup> Now these are the chief of the province that dwelt in Jerusalem: but in the cities of Judah dwelt every one in his possession in their cities, to wit, Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the Nethinims, and the children of Solomon’s servants.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/nehemiah/11#v4)</sup> And at Jerusalem dwelt certain of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin. Of the children of Judah; Athaiah the son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalaleel, of the children of Perez;
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/nehemiah/11#v5)</sup> And Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Col–hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of Shiloni.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/nehemiah/11#v6)</sup> All the sons of Perez that dwelt at Jerusalem were four hundred threescore and eight valiant men.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/nehemiah/11#v7)</sup> And these are the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jesaiah.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/nehemiah/11#v8)</sup> And after him Gabbai, Sallai, nine hundred twenty and eight.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/nehemiah/11#v9)</sup> And Joel the son of Zichri was their overseer: and Judah the son of Senuah was second over the city.

- These verses name the children of Judah and Benjamin who dwelt in Jerusalem: from Judah, Athaiah of the line of Perez, and Maaseiah of the line of Shiloni; from Benjamin, Sallu and his brethren.
- Four hundred threescore and eight valiant men of the sons of Perez dwelt in Jerusalem, and Joel and Judah were set as overseers over the city. These are a name register, the record of the families that repopulated the city.

**[Nehemiah 11:10-14](/bible/nehemiah/11#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/nehemiah/11#v10)</sup> Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/nehemiah/11#v11)</sup> Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, was the ruler of the house of God.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/nehemiah/11#v12)</sup> And their brethren that did the work of the house were eight hundred twenty and two: and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchiah,
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/nehemiah/11#v13)</sup> And his brethren, chief of the fathers, two hundred forty and two: and Amashai the son of Azareel, the son of Ahasai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer,
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/nehemiah/11#v14)</sup> And their brethren, mighty men of valour, an hundred twenty and eight: and their overseer was Zabdiel, the son of one of the great men.

- These verses name the priests: Jedaiah, Jachin, and Seraiah, who was the ruler of the house of God, with their brethren that did the work of the house numbering eight hundred twenty and two.
- More priests are named after them, with their chief men, and their overseer was Zabdiel, one of the great men. This is the register of the priesthood that served in the holy city.

**[Nehemiah 11:15-24](/bible/nehemiah/11#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/nehemiah/11#v15)</sup> Also of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hashub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni;
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/nehemiah/11#v16)</sup> And Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the chief of the Levites, had the oversight of the outward business of the house of God.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/nehemiah/11#v17)</sup> And Mattaniah the son of Micha, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, was the principal to begin the thanksgiving in prayer: and Bakbukiah the second among his brethren, and Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/nehemiah/11#v18)</sup> All the Levites in the holy city were two hundred fourscore and four.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/nehemiah/11#v19)</sup> Moreover the porters, Akkub, Talmon, and their brethren that kept the gates, were an hundred seventy and two.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/nehemiah/11#v20)</sup> And the residue of Israel, of the priests, and the Levites, were in all the cities of Judah, every one in his inheritance.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/nehemiah/11#v21)</sup> But the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel: and Ziha and Gispa were over the Nethinims.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/nehemiah/11#v22)</sup> The overseer also of the Levites at Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micha. Of the sons of Asaph, the singers were over the business of the house of God.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/nehemiah/11#v23)</sup> For it was the king’s commandment concerning them, that a certain portion should be for the singers, due for every day.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/nehemiah/11#v24)</sup> And Pethahiah the son of Meshezabeel, of the children of Zerah the son of Judah, was at the king’s hand in all matters concerning the people.

- These verses name the Levites and their duties: Shemaiah and others, and the chief Levites who had oversight of the outward business of the house of God, and Mattaniah who was the principal to begin the thanksgiving in prayer.
- The porters that kept the gates are numbered, and the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel. The singers were over the business of the house of God, for it was the king's commandment that a certain portion should be for the singers due for every day.

  - **[Nehemiah 11:23](/bible/nehemiah/11#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/nehemiah/11#v23)</sup> For it was the king’s commandment concerning them, that a certain portion should be for the singers, due for every day.

    A certain portion for the singers due for every day was set by the king's commandment, showing that even under a foreign king the temple service was provided for.

**[Nehemiah 11:25-36](/bible/nehemiah/11#v25)**

> <sup>[25](/bible/nehemiah/11#v25)</sup> And for the villages, with their fields, some of the children of Judah dwelt at Kirjath–arba, and in the villages thereof, and at Dibon, and in the villages thereof, and at Jekabzeel, and in the villages thereof,
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/nehemiah/11#v26)</sup> And at Jeshua, and at Moladah, and at Beth–phelet,
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/nehemiah/11#v27)</sup> And at Hazar–shual, and at Beer–sheba, and in the villages thereof,
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/nehemiah/11#v28)</sup> And at Ziklag, and at Mekonah, and in the villages thereof,
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/nehemiah/11#v29)</sup> And at En–rimmon, and at Zareah, and at Jarmuth,
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/nehemiah/11#v30)</sup> Zanoah, Adullam, and in their villages, at Lachish, and the fields thereof, at Azekah, and in the villages thereof. And they dwelt from Beer–sheba unto the valley of Hinnom.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/nehemiah/11#v31)</sup> The children also of Benjamin from Geba dwelt at Michmash, and Aija, and Beth–el, and in their villages,
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/nehemiah/11#v32)</sup> And at Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/nehemiah/11#v33)</sup> Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/nehemiah/11#v34)</sup> Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/nehemiah/11#v35)</sup> Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/nehemiah/11#v36)</sup> And of the Levites were divisions in Judah, and in Benjamin.

- These verses list the villages where the children of Judah dwelt, from Kirjatharba to Beersheba and its valleys, and where the children of Benjamin dwelt, from Geba to Michmash and the surrounding towns.
- Certain divisions of the Levites in Judah were joined to Benjamin. This closes the register of where the returned people settled across the land, each in his inheritance.
